interest: Covers Axis diplomacy in Spain: Minister Suma's unrealistic peace scenarios, Manila consulate crisis, and OSS surveillance of Japanese press agents.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.20252) documents U.S. surveillance and intelligence assessments of Japanese diplomatic, military, and espionage activities in Spain between January 1945 and May 1946. Centered on communications from the American Embassy in Madrid to the Secretary of State, the records feature extensive intelligence obtained from confidential informants regarding Japanese Minister Yakichiro Suma. The reports detail Suma's assessments of the secret Franco-Soviet treaty, prospects for a separate German-Soviet rapprochement, damage from Allied air raids on Tokyo and the dispersal of Japanese industry underground, Japanese naval intentions, and negotiations in Moscow to preserve the Soviet-Japanese non-aggression pact. The file also chronicles the diplomatic tension following Japanese attacks on the Spanish Consulate General in Manila, OSS evaluations of Japanese propaganda newspapers smuggled through local contacts of Yomiuri-Hochi correspondent Kuninosuke Matsuo, and post-war censorship intercepts concerning former legation espionage officer Fumio Miura.

subfiles.about: Reports intelligence from Japanese Minister Yakichiro Suma regarding secret clauses in the Franco-Soviet pact, potential German-Soviet rapprochement, and impending European political maneuvers.
subfiles.from: Carlton J. H. Hayes (American Embassy, Madrid)
subfiles.summary: Airgram A-10: Suma alleges secret Franco-Soviet basing rights in France and North Africa, and claims Germany's Ardennes offensive aimed at a Nazi-Soviet peace allied with Japan.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-10 from Embassy Madrid on Suma's Remarks Concerning Franco-Russian Agreement and German-Soviet Peace Prospects

subfiles.about: Instructs Embassy Madrid to repeat its secret airgram A-10 regarding Suma's claims to the U.S. diplomatic missions in Paris and Tangier.
subfiles.from: Department of State (Acting Secretary of State [Joseph C. Grew])
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 161 instructs Madrid to repeat Airgram A-10 on Suma's Franco-Soviet claims to Paris and Tangier.
subfiles.title: State Department Telegram No. 161 Instructing Madrid to Repeat Airgram A-10 to Paris and Tangier

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording intelligence material concerning Heinrich Bauer filed under decimal file 862.20252/1-1245.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference on intelligence concerning 'PEP' and Heinrich Bauer, filed under German espionage file 862.20252/1-1245.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Intelligence Material Transmitted Concerning Heinrich Bauer

subfiles.about: Reports Japanese Minister Suma's growing anxiety over American advances in the Pacific and Japanese efforts to remodel its aviation equipment.
subfiles.from: Carlton J. H. Hayes (American Embassy, Madrid)
subfiles.summary: Airgram A-21: Suma shows anxiety over the US Pacific advance and says Japan is reorganizing its aircraft equipment.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-21 from Embassy Madrid on Suma's Concern Over Pacific Advances and Japanese Aviation Reorganization

subfiles.about: Transmits a Japanese newspaper obtained by an Embassy informant from a Spanish contact employed by Japanese correspondent Kuninosuke Matsuo.
subfiles.from: Chargé d'Affaires ad interim (American Embassy, Madrid)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 4142: Madrid forwards a Japanese newspaper obtained via agent 'X' from a contact of correspondent Matsuo.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4142 from Embassy Madrid Transmitting Japanese Newspaper Obtained Through Legation Contact

subfiles.about: Returns the copy and translations of the Japanese newspaper Baibai Hochi, concluding it holds no immediate intelligence value.
subfiles.from: Bernard A. Towell, X-2 Branch, Office of Strategic Services (OSS)
subfiles.summary: Towell (OSS) returns a 1943 Japanese newspaper and translations, finding no current intelligence value since its stories were already publicized.
subfiles.title: OSS Memorandum from Bernard A. Towell Returning Japanese Newspaper and Translations to State Department
subfiles.to: Clifton P. English, Department of State

subfiles.about: Provides English translations of the front-page headlines of the October 20, 1943 issue of the Japanese newspaper Baibai Hochi.
subfiles.summary: OSS translation of Baibai Hochi's October 1943 front page: Japanese army operations in China/Burma, and Bose's Indian Government in Singapore.
subfiles.title: OSS Translation of First Page Headlines from Baibai Hochi of October 20, 1943
subfiles.to: Clifton P. English, Department of State

subfiles.about: A printed Japanese newspaper issue of the Baibai Hochi (Yomiuri-Hochi) dated October 20, 1943, acquired by U.S. intelligence in Spain.
subfiles.summary: Four pages of the October 1943 Baibai Hochi/Yomiuri-Hochi newspaper, covering Japanese military operations and Subhas Chandra Bose in Singapore.
subfiles.title: Japanese Newspaper Issue of Baibai Hochi / Yomiuri-Hochi, October 20, 1943

subfiles.about: Reports statements by Japanese Minister Suma on Tokyo air raid destruction, underground industrial relocation, naval strategy, and Soviet-Japanese diplomatic talks.
subfiles.summary: Airgram A-143: Suma says Tokyo raids destroyed 10,000 homes but spared factories moved underground, and predicts a Japanese naval ambush and a renewed Soviet pact.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-143 from Embassy Madrid on Suma's Remarks on Tokyo Bombings, Military Readiness, and Soviet Talks

subfiles.about: Reports Suma's statements regarding escalating Tokyo bombings, underground production, and Soviet diplomatic repercussions if Spain breaks relations over the Manila consulate attack.
subfiles.summary: Airgram: Suma repeats that underground factories limit Tokyo bombing damage, and warns Spain that severing Japan ties over the Manila consulate attack risks Soviet retaliation.
subfiles.title: Secret Airgram from Embassy Madrid on Tokyo Bombings, Soviet Geopolitics, and Spanish-Japanese Tensions over Manila

subfiles.about: Transmits an intercepted Japanese letter sent from Kobe to former legation First Secretary Fumio Miura, who had engaged in espionage in Spain.
subfiles.from: Chargé d'Affaires ad interim (American Embassy, Madrid)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 1914: Madrid forwards an intercepted letter to Fumio Miura, a former Legation secretary active in wartime Japanese espionage.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1914 from Embassy Madrid Transmitting Intercepted Japanese Letter Addressed to Fumio Miura

subfiles.about: An intercepted Japanese letter sent from Kobe to former Japanese diplomat and espionage operative Fumio Miura in Madrid.
subfiles.summary: Intercepted 1946 letter from Kobe to former Japanese Legation secretary Fumio Miura, reflecting postwar monitoring of ex-Axis diplomatic personnel in Spain.
subfiles.title: Intercepted Japanese Letter Addressed to Former Legation First Secretary Fumio Miura
